name: Crown of the Earth
summary: At Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip prepares young night elves for their departure from Shadowglen. They draw sacred water in a rite that recalls Mount Hyjal and the immortality their people surrendered there.

sections.title: A Lesson in Recent History
sections.body: Before young night elves leave Shadowglen, their elders teach them what their people lost. At Mount Hyjal, the kaldorei sacrificed the World Tree Nordrassil to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. The blast took their ageless immortality and sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip teaches this history through a rite, so the novices leave with humility and purpose in a changing world.

sections.title: Waters of the Well
sections.body: You draw water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil with a crystal phial. Moonwell waters bear remnants of the ancient Well of Eternity. Druids channel their restorative power into the wild, while Sentinels honor the wells as tranquil shrines to Elune. The kaldorei remain wary of arcane sorcery, which is forbidden. The wellspring sustains their land, yet recalls the reckless magic that nearly broke the world.

aliases: who gives crown of the earth
faq.answer: Tenaron Stormgrip lives high in Aldrassil's upper boughs in Shadowglen. He mentors young night elves nearing the end of basic training, teaching their solemn history through rites before they travel onward into Teldrassil.

faq.q: What is the purpose of collecting moonwell water?
faq.answer: Filling the crystal phial begins a practical and ceremonial journey. Moonwell waters hold ancient magic that druids use to nourish the land, and the rite teaches young kaldorei their society's sacred obligations.

faq.q: Why did the night elves lose their immortality?
faq.answer: During the Third War, the night elves unleashed the ancestral power woven into the World Tree Nordrassil to destroy Archimonde atop Mount Hyjal. The sacrifice destroyed the Legion's vanguard, but cost the night elves their eternal youth and immunity to disease.

Moonwells hold diluted essences linked to the Well of Eternity. Druids and priestesses channel their energies for healing, blessing, and communion with nature. The kaldorei forbid arcane sorcery because reckless magic caused catastrophes in ancient history.

faq.q: Where does this quest chain lead next?
aliases: what comes after crown of the earth
faq.answer: After you return the filled phial, Tenaron sends you to Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. There, you fill phials at other moonwells across Teldrassil for the druids of Darnassus, and finally for Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm.

faq.q: Where is the moonwell for this quest located?
faq.answer: The moonwell lies a short walk north of Aldrassil's great boughs, among the woods of Shadowglen.

angles.text: As a night elf, this rite marks your passage out of Shadowglen. It ties your path to the sacrifice atop Mount Hyjal and your duty to safeguard Teldrassil.
As a druid, you know moonwells as essential tools of the Cenarion circle. They offer purified conduits of nature's energy to tend the forest's balance.
As a priest, you honor Elune at moonwells, reflective shrines where the waters are consecrated beneath the Mother Moon's gaze.
